MAN ARRESTED FOR IMPAIRED DRIVING TWICE IN LESS THAN TWO HOURS AND ACCUSED OF BRIBING AN OFFICER
(Nov 26)
A 50-year-old man is facing multiple criminal charges after being arrested twice for impaired driving in Paradise on Wednesday afternoon.
At approximately 1:15 p.m. on November 25, RNC officers received a complaint of an impaired driver in the Topsail Road area of Paradise.
Officers located the man at a local bar, where he was arrested for impaired driving. Subsequent breathalyzer testing registered more than three times the legal limit.
Police impounded his vehicle, suspended his driver’s licence and charged him with impaired driving.
Less than two hours later, at approximately 3:11 p.m., officers returned to the man’s residence to inform him of an additional charge of bribery of a police officer.
Upon arrival, officers noticed the garage door was wide open and a Corvette was missing.
Police then observed the man driving past them in his Corvette. He was stopped and arrested for impaired driving for the second time that afternoon.
The man now faces multiple charges of impaired driving, operating a vehicle while over the legal limit, driving while suspended and bribery of a police officer.
The Corvette was also seized, and the man was transported to the city lockup, where he awaits an appearance before a judge.

NUMEROUS VEHICLES IMPOUNDED FOLLOWING TRAFFIC STOPS WEDNESDAY NIGHT
(Nov 26)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) seized and impounded numerous vehicles following a series of traffic stops Wednesday night, November 25th.
At 9:25 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop on Topsail Road, where a 30-year-old man was charged with driving while suspended. The driver also had $3,534 in outstanding fines.
At 9:35 p.m., officers conducted another traffic stop near McDonald’s on Topsail Road, where a 29-year-old man was charged with operating a vehicle without valid insurance.
Just five minutes later, at 9:40 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop on St. Thomas Line. A 50-year-old man registered a “WARN” on an approved roadside screening device and was issued a seven-day driving suspension. He was also ticketed for failing to transfer vehicle ownership.
At 11:19 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop near Subway on Hamlyn Road after determining the driver was prohibited from driving anywhere in Canada following an impaired driving conviction.
The man was arrested and charged with driving while prohibited and issued a ticket for driving while suspended. He was transported to the city lockup to await a court appearance.
All vehicles involved in the above incidents were seized and impounded by police

THREE WANTED INDIVIDUALS ARRESTED BY RNC FOLLOWING TWO SEPARATE INCIDENTS
(Nov 26)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) arrested three individuals on outstanding arrest warrants following two separate incidents on Wednesday, November 25th.
At 4:05 p.m., officers received a complaint of a wanted person in the area of Conways Brook Road. Following an investigation, police located a 30-year-old man and a 28-year-old woman, both of whom were wanted on outstanding arrest warrants.
Both individuals were arrested and charged with failure to appear.
Later that evening, at 7:07 p.m., officers responded to a complaint of unknown trouble at a residence on Bastow Court. Police learned that an intoxicated woman had been at the residence but had since left in a taxi.
Officers later located the 41-year-old woman and arrested her on an outstanding arrest warrant.
All three individuals were transported to the city lockup, where they await their respective court appearances.

GOV NL PUTS PAUSE ON PROPOSED FLAVOURED VAPE RESTRICTIONS
(Nov 25th)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador is putting a pause on the proposed changes to the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act, which would introduce restrictions on flavoured vaping products.
The decision will allow additional time for public and stakeholder consultations before the government moves forward with the proposed legislation.
The proposed restrictions have not yet been implemented, and no changes are currently in effect.
Further details are expected as the consultation process continues.

RCMP INVESTIGATING BREAK-IN AT 50 PLUS CLUB
(Nov 25th)
Bay St. George RCMP is investigating a break and enter at the Stephenville Crossing 50 Plus Club earlier this month after significant damage was reported to the building and a nearby property.
Shortly before 4:45 a.m. on November 15, police responded to a report of a break and enter at the club on Maple Street.
Police say the suspect or suspects caused extensive damage to an exterior power pole in an effort to cut electricity to the building before forcing their way inside.
Cash was stolen from a register, and two video lottery terminals were opened. However, the machines were empty at the time of the break-in.
The damage to the power pole also resulted in exterior damage to a neighbouring property.
The investigation is ongoing with assistance from the RCMP Forensic Identification Section.
Anyone with information that could assist investigators, including video surveillance or dash camera footage from the area during the early morning hours of November 15, 2026, is asked to contact Bay St. George RCMP at 709-643-2118 or call 1-800-709-RCMP (7267).
Information can also be provided anonymously through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

COUNTRY RIBBON RECEIVES $492,000 TO ELECTRIFY FEED MILL BOILER
(Nov 25th)
The provincial government has announced a $492,000 investment through the Green Transition Fund to support Country Ribbon’s Feed Mill Boiler Electrification Project.
The project will replace the boiler’s use of fuel oil with electricity, reducing annual fuel consumption by an estimated 175,000 litres and carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 448 metric tonnes each year.
The upgrade is also expected to improve energy efficiency, operational reliability and long-term energy cost stability.
Country Ribbon employs more than 350 Newfoundlanders and Labradorians and operates the province’s only feed mill and large-scale federally registered poultry processing plant. It is also the only fully integrated poultry operation in Atlantic Canada.
The provincial government says the investment will help strengthen local poultry production, improve supply chains and increase the availability of locally produced food.

RNC SEIZE OVER HALF A KILOGRAM OF COCAINE DURING ST. JOHN’S DRUG INVESTIGATION
(Nov 25th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) seized more than half a kilogram of suspected cocaine, prescription pills and cash while executing a search warrant at a residence in St. John’s.
On Tuesday, November 24, officers with the RNC’s Weapons and Drug Enforcement Unit (WDEU) executed a search warrant at a west-end property as part of an ongoing drug trafficking investigation.
During the search, officers located and seized over 0.5 kilograms of cocaine, prescription pills, cash and drug paraphernalia.
James Kelloway, 59, was arrested and charged with four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. He was held for court.
A second male was also arrested and subsequently released. Additional drug-related charges are expected for both men, pending the results of drug testing.
The investigation remains ongoing.
The RNC’s Weapons and Drug Enforcement Unit says it remains dedicated to removing illegal weapons and drugs from communities through overt and covert proactive operations.
Anyone with information regarding criminal activity is asked to contact the RNC at 709-729-8000.

MOTORISTS URGED TO USE CAUTION DUE TO SNOW-COVERED ROADS
(Nov 25th)
Motorists travelling across parts of Central and Western Newfoundland are being urged to use caution this morning as winter driving conditions are being reported on several highways.
A look at highway cameras this morning shows snow-covered and partially snow-covered roadways across portions of Central and Western Newfoundland, the northeast coast and the Northern Peninsula.
Areas experiencing winter driving conditions include Grand Falls-Windsor, Corner Brook, Rocky Harbour and Daniel’s Harbour.
Meanwhile, roadways around Lewisporte appear mostly wet, with a light dusting of snow visible along the shoulders.
The RCMP NL is also warning motorists about slippery road conditions on the Northern Peninsula, particularly along Routes 430 and 431 in the Rocky Harbour and Gros Morne National Park areas.
Police are advising motorists to consider delaying any immediate travel plans. Those who must travel are urged to exercise extreme caution and drive according to road and weather conditions.
Motorists are reminded to reduce their speed, allow additional time for travel and remain prepared for changing road conditions.

ONE PERSON TAKEN TO HOSPITAL AFTER KENMOUNT ROAD COLLISION
(Nov 25th)
Emergency crews responded to a two-vehicle collision on Kenmount Road in St. John’s Tuesday evening. 
Just before 8:45 p.m (Nov 24th), personnel with the St. John’s Regional Fire Department (SJRFD), Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) and NL Health Services were called to the scene in front of Starbucks, between Pippy Place and the Team Gushue Highway.
Upon arrival, first responders located two SUVs that had sustained extensive damage. The collision appeared to have occurred in the eastbound lanes of Kenmount Road.
Firefighters and paramedics assessed those involved for potential injuries. An SJRFD Captain confirmed at the scene that the sole occupant of both vehicles were being assessed for what were believed to be non-serious injuries. At least one of the individuals were later transported to the hospital via ambulance. 
Traffic was reduced to one lane in each direction as emergency crews dealt with the scene and arrangements were made to remove the damaged vehicles.

STOLEN VEHICLE - WESTERN NEWFOUNDLAND
(Nov 24th)
~ 4:10 p.m; The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is investigating a stolen vehicle in Corner Brook.
Operational Patrol Services responded to a report of a stolen pickup truck from a property on Humber Road in Corner Brook around 6:45 a.m. today.
The vehicle is a grey 2023 Dodge Ram with Newfoundland and Labrador license plate CM7 376. (Please see attached photo).
The RNC has received an increase in reports of thefts from vehicles in the Corner Brook region recently. To protect yourself from being targeted:
- Lock your car doors and being mindful of where you place your keys.
- Bring items of value inside your home where they can be locked away securely.
- Do not leave spare keys in vehicles or close to open or unlocked windows and doors.
Park in high-traffic, well-lit areas.
Anyone with information to assist the investigation is asked to contact the RNC at 709-637-4100. Crimes in progress should be reported by contacting 911.

FOUR ARRESTED FOLLOWING THEFT INVESTIGATION IN ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 24th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) made four arrests following an investigation into a reported stolen purse in St. John’s.
At approximately 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, November 23, officers with Operational Patrol Services responded to a reported theft in the city’s centre city area.
The investigation led officers to a residence on Hatcher Street, where the stolen property was recovered.
A 33-year-old female was charged with possession of property obtained by crime and breach of probation. She was also arrested on an outstanding warrant.
Three other individuals were arrested at the residence on outstanding warrants, including a 37-year-old male, a 35-year-old female and a 41-year-old female.
Two of the individuals were held for court, while the other two were released to appear at a later date.
The RNC continues to encourage anyone who witnesses suspicious activity to report it directly to police by calling 709-729-8000. Crimes in progress should be reported by calling 911.

MISSING LEWISPORTE MAN LOCATED SAFE
(Nov 24)
The RCMP has confirmed that a missing 45-year-old man from Lewisporte has been located and is safe following a search in the area.
The Exploits Search and Rescue Team deployed its drone team to assist with search efforts. The man was ultimately located outside the search area, bringing the search to a successful conclusion.
The search and rescue team thanked local residents and the RCMP for their partnership in bringing the man home, as well as Burnt Bay Construction for allowing the team to use its parking lot to conduct drone operations.
The RCMP also thanked the public for their concern and assistance.

MAN ARRESTED FOLLOWING COLLISION IN CHAPEL ARM
(Nov 24th)
A 52-year-old man is facing impaired driving charges following a two-vehicle collision and alleged hit-and-run in Chapel Arm on Monday evening (Nov. 23).
Just before 6:30 p.m., Placentia-Whitbourne RCMP responded to a reported collision involving two vehicles on Main Road.
Upon arrival, police spoke with the driver of one vehicle, who reported that the second vehicle had collided with them before fleeing the scene. No injuries were reported.
Police located a 52-year-old man and a vehicle matching the description, which had sustained damage, at a nearby residence.
The man was arrested for impaired operation and transported to the detachment, where testing confirmed his blood alcohol level was more than twice the legal limit.
His vehicle was seized and impounded, and his driver’s licence was suspended.
He was later released under conditions and is expected to appear in provincial court in January 2027 to answer to charges of impaired operation, impaired operation over 80 mg% and failure to stop at the scene of an accident.
